published_statement: 1208.5399 Sec. 5.1 (p.44): classically 'the energy density can be made arbitrarily negative at any given point'; 'The corresponding quantum theory was discussed in [29] [= FO 0708.2450] for the case of Minkowski space. It was found that the nonminimally coupled field can sustain large negative energy densities for long periods of time. ... one-particle states with negative energy density near the origin ... By a scaling argument these can be taken to have any desired spacetime extent, although the magnitude is correspondingly reduced. However, we may tensor together as many of these one-particle states as we wish, with respect to which the energy density is additive (as this is a free theory). Thus states of arbitrarily negative energy density can be sustained over arbitrarily large spacetime volumes.' p.45: 'However, there is a cost. The overall energy of these states is positive, and grows more rapidly than the scales characterising the negative energy density effect produced. ... one can establish QEI bounds for the nonminimally coupled field that are state-dependent [29] ... This is still a comparatively new development'. Sec. 5.2 (p.45), first bullet: 'One cannot expect state-independent QEIs to hold; as mentioned, these can even fail in the nonminimally coupled theory. ... However, it is possible that modified QEIs hold'. Sec. 5.2 opening: 'similar results [QEIs] hold in a large class of conformal field theories in two dimensions. The situation for interacting fields is more complicated ... not so much is known.' PRIMARY (FO 0708.2450 Sec. 3 summary, p.8): 'to any bounded subset O of Minkowski space and arbitrary constant rho_0 > 0 there is a Hadamard state in which the expected energy density is less than -rho_0 throughout O. In particular any smearing rho_quant(f) with a non-negative compactly supported distribution f is unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states.' FO conclusion (p.20): 'we have shown (at least for massless fields in four-dimensional Minkowski space) that the non-minimally coupled scalar field with xi > 0 admits states with arbitrarily large negative energy density over arbitrarily large bounded spacetime regions. Thus the non-minimally coupled field cannot obey QEIs of the type previously studied in the literature, in which there is a state-independent lower bound.'
published_hypotheses: H1 free (non-self-interacting) real scalar field; additivity of the energy density over tensor products uses freeness ('as this is a free theory', 1208.5399 p.44)

H2 coupling xi > 0 (FO Sec. 3 'the massless quantised scalar quantum field with xi > 0'; the construction's sign enters through eq.(29) rho(0,0) = -xi(2 kappa)^4/(3 pi^2)); 1208.5399 Sec. 5.1 does not state the sign
H3 MASSLESS field (FO Sec. 3; conclusion 'at least for massless fields'); the scaling step (FO eq.(27)) uses masslessness; 1208.5399 Sec. 5.1 does not state it
H4 four-dimensional MINKOWSKI space (1208.5399: 'for the case of Minkowski space'; FO: '(3+1)-dimensional Minkowski space'); not proved on a curved background
H5 states: Hadamard (FO: 'Owing to the rapid decay of h_kappa, Psi_kappa is Hadamard'); the energy density is normal-ordered relative to the Minkowski vacuum

H6 the quantity shown unbounded below is any smearing of the energy density with a non-negative compactly supported f (spacetime), hence a fortiori worldline averages; the state-dependent QEI (FO Thm 4.2/4.3) is proved for timelike GEODESICS and 0 < xi <= 1/4 (curved: globally hyperbolic)

H7 the price: the witness states' total energy grows faster than the negative-energy scale (FO eq.(34): <H> > (tau')^3 2 pi^2 rho_0/(xi kappa^3 tau^3)); a negative-energy region is bought with disproportionate positive energy

H8 (Sec. 5.2 clause) interacting fields: 'one cannot expect' state-independent QEIs -- an EXPECTATION, stated beside the in-source counterexample of 2D CFTs and the caveat 'it is possible that modified QEIs hold'; not a theorem

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (17 checks, exit 0; output in rederive/1208.5399-sec5.1.out). A1: FO eq.(28), the energy density at the spatial origin of Psi_kappa, re-derived symbolically from dmu = d^3k/((2pi)^3 2|k|) and rho = |F'|^2 - 4 xi Re(conj(F) F'') -- exact match. A2: eq.(29) rho(0,0) = -xi(2 kappa)^4/(3 pi^2). B1/B2: normalisation 1 and eq.(26) <H> = 2 kappa/3. C1: scaling eq.(27) exact. C2: continuity ball (xi = 1/6, kappa = 1: rho(t,0) <= rho(0,0)/2 for |t| <= 0.1). D1: tensoring/additivity -- in (a^dag(h))^n/sqrt(n!) Omega the one-particle density matrix is n|h><h| and pair terms vanish, n = 1..4 on an explicit Fock space. E1-E3 (EXTENSION, computed here, not in the sources): rho(0,0) = C^2(A2^2 + 4 xi A1 A3); A1A3/A2^2 = 3(K+1)^2/(8K) -> oo for h = e^-k + K^-3 e^(-k/K); normalised witnesses rho(0,0) ~ -8.2, -8.1, -8.6 at xi = -1/100, -1/1000, -1/10 -- so the no-state-independent-QEI conclusion extends to xi < 0 (massless, 4D Minkowski) by FO's own argument. F1/F2: FO's single-exponential state gives rho(0,0) = +8 kappa^4/(15 pi^2) at xi = -1/10 (negative only for xi < -1/6), so FO's printed state does not cover xi < 0. G1-G4: section attribution against the saved page text (5.1 quote verbatim; 'one cannot expect' is 5.2; 5.1 never says 'state-independent QEI'; 5.1 scoped to 'the case of Minkowski space'). Not checked: FO Thm 4.2 (state-dependent bound) and their H-bound analysis (Sec. 5.2 of FO), which the tree does not use here.

later_literature.ref: Bostelmann, Cadamuro & Fewster, 'Quantum Energy Inequality for the Massive Ising Model', arXiv:1304.7682 (PRD 88 (2013) 025019)
later_literature.what: Narrows the Sec. 5.2 interacting-field clause, not the NMC clause: 'A Quantum Energy Inequality (QEI) is derived for the massive Ising model, giving a state-independent lower bound ... the first QEI to be established for an interacting quantum field theory with nontrivial S-matrix' (1+1D, S2 = -1). The model has one-particle states with negative energy density, but the energy density 'is not additive with respect to tensor products' -- 'It is intriguing that the interaction is responsible for maintaining the QEI'. So the free-field tensoring mechanism behind Sec. 5.1 is exactly what fails there, and 'interacting fields: no state-independent QEI is expected' (specthm.py:1046-1048, 2160-2161) is not general. Caveat stated by the authors: the smeared identity is 'expected' to be rigorous for Hadamard states of the Majorana field; 1+1 dimensions only.

later_literature.ref: Fliss & Rolph, 'Curious QNEIs from QNEC: New Bounds on Null Energy in Quantum Field Theory', arXiv:2510.26247 (v2 Apr 2026)
later_literature.what: Confirms the NMC non-existence in the null direction too: 'the non-minimally coupled scalar field for which one can construct states of arbitrarily negative expectation value of the timelike or null-contracted stress tensor, regardless of the domain over which it is smeared [23, 24]' and notes this bites 'the free scalar CFT even in flat space' (improvement term). Extends the interacting side: derives 'the first QEIs in a large class of interacting theories in greater than two dimensions' -- null-null component, smeared over a null interval AND uniformly over all d-2 transverse directions (divergent transverse volume), QNEC assumed, state-independent only through O(eps_u^0) (their fn.15). Not a timelike-worldline energy-density QEI, so it does not directly bear on the tree's duration theorem, but it is further evidence that 'interacting => no state-independent bound' is not a rule.

The primary source of Sec. 5.1 (earlier than the lectures, read here as the theorem itself): construction for xi > 0, massless, 4D Minkowski, re-derived in full by the rederive script (eqs.(26)-(29), (27), (33)); state-dependent QEI Thm 4.2 for 0 < xi <= 1/4 on globally hyperbolic spacetimes along timelike geodesics; energy cost eq.(34). Their conclusion expects an absolute NMC version 'can also be adapted' (expected, not done).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. The conclusion is a construction inside a free-field model, not a fit to data: there is no measured input whose later value could move it (data rows 1-2). What the 2012 lecture and the 2007 paper lacked were RESULTS, not data, and they cut differently for the two clauses the tree merges. (a) NMC clause: nothing later contradicts it; Fliss-Rolph 2025 restates it (timelike and null, any smearing domain) and FO's construction re-derives exactly here. Its limit is scope, which FO themselves print ('at least for massless fields in four-dimensional Minkowski space', xi > 0): massive fields and curved backgrounds are not covered, and xi < 0 is not covered by the source (closed here by a computation, E1-E3). Having more data would not change it. (b) Interacting clause: in 2012 'not so much is known' (Sec. 5.2) and the lecture explicitly states an expectation, hedged ('it is possible that modified QEIs hold'). Later work did supply what was missing: Bostelmann-Cadamuro-Fewster 2013 proved a state-independent QEI for the massive Ising model (1+1D), precisely because interaction breaks the tensor-product additivity that powers Sec. 5.1; Fliss-Rolph 2025 give transversely-integrated state-independent null bounds for interacting CFTs in d > 2. So for the interacting clause M's hypothesis is borne out in the narrow sense that the 2012 authors lacked these results and the expectation, read as a blanket rule, is now too strong -- but the author called it an expectation, it was never a theorem, and nothing later establishes a state-independent timelike QEI for a generic 4D interacting theory either: the question is OPEN, not reversed. Neither development helps a warp corridor: the NMC escape carries FO's energy cost (eq.(34)) and the interacting-field QEIs found are ones that HOLD (i.e. constrain), in 2D or on transversely-integrated null data.
grade_evidence: The NMC statement is correct and re-derived: FO eqs.(26)-(29), scaling (27) and tensor additivity (33) all reproduce exactly (rederive A-D, ALL PASS), so for a free MASSLESS xi > 0 scalar in 4D MINKOWSKI no state-independent lower bound exists on any non-negative smearing of the energy density. The tree uses it more broadly than the source proves: (1) unsigned 'nonminimally coupled' (bounds.py:283-285, achievable.py:155-157, 252-253, 370-371, noise.py:222) where the source has xi > 0 -- the xi < 0 gap is closed here by computation (E1-E3), not by the source; (2) masslessness dropped everywhere (massive case OPEN); (3) Minkowski dropped at bounds.py:283-285 ('DOCKET 53 Route B's own field' -- right field, but Route B's background is curved and non-existence is not proved there; qeihps.py:85-88 records it, bounds.py does not). (4) The interacting-field clause is Sec. 5.2, not 5.1 (achievable.py:251-255, specthm.py:1046-1048, 2357 -- already flagged by noise.py:301-302), is an expectation in the source, and is narrowed by the source's own 2D-CFT remark and by the massive-Ising state-independent QEI (1304.7682, READ). None of this moves a tree verdict: every rests_on_it site uses the result as a LIMITATION on the tree's own refusal ('not a theorem about matter in general'; VERDICT_KIND = 'SURVEY'; H_M0 scope), and for that use the Minkowski massless xi = 1/6 case suffices. No computed contradiction, so not WRONG; no moved datum, so not DATA-DEPENDENT.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners scope the NMC clause as the source does (xi > 0 or, citing this computation, xi != 0; massless; 4D Minkowski) and attribute the interacting-field remark to Sec. 5.2 as an expectation with the 2D/Ising exceptions named. To WRONG for the NMC clause: a state-independent lower bound on some non-negative smearing of the massless xi > 0 energy density in Minkowski, which would contradict FO's re-derived construction -- none found. To WRONG for the tree's application: a proof that the xi = 1/6 field on HPS's specific curved background DOES obey a state-independent bound would not make the statement wrong but would remove the escape at Route B. A proof (or disproof) of state-independent timelike QEIs for massive NMC fields, or for a 4D interacting theory, would settle the two OPEN edges.
